label: copy-phase input token e (recall position >= 2)
explanation: Fires when the letter e is fed back as input during the copy phase, i.e. the model just output an e (original tokens 1..L-2), at recall_idx >= 2. Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and essentially never on any other input token. Silent or near-silent when e is the first copied-back token (recall_idx 1, e = orig(0)); that case is the only real source of false positives for the plain e-in-copy-phase rule (P 0.82 -> 1.00 once excluded). Magnitude is roughly uniform (median 4.5); from the examples, the weakest activations come at early recall positions (e.g. e as orig(1) about 0.45 of max), and the strongest come in the middle-to-late copy phase, especially on the first of a repeated e e pair (about 0.97-1.0 of max).

issues: Test split: P 1.000, R 0.993, F1 0.997, mass recall 0.9998, correlation 0.986, with 0 false positives. All 506 test misses together hold 0.0% of activation mass.

The misses form one class plus a little noise. Most are e at recall_idx 1 (e is orig(0)) with tiny activations of about 0.01-0.06 of max, which fits 'silent or nearly silent'. The rest are a few scattered ~0.01 activations on the token right after an e (for example '1' and 'n'). None of this is a meaningful systematic gap.

Phase claims hold. Dev shows 0 activations in the original phase and 0 on the delimiter, and the copy phase holds 100% of the mass. in_tok e holds 100% of the mass; other tokens fire only on 4-23 steps each.

The magnitude claims are roughly consistent. Mass per active step at recall_idx 2 (0.163/16441) is about 26% lower than at recall_idx 3 (0.220/16100), which fits 'weakest early in the copy phase'. The 'e e pair is strongest' claim is hedged as coming from examples only, and I did not check it quantitatively.
